newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece to sign oil prospecting pacts next week.
newsitem.headline: Greece to sign oil prospecting pacts next week.

text.p: Greece will sign final agreements next week with three international companies for oil prospecting in western Greece, a Ministry of Development press officer said on Friday.

State-owned Public Petroleum Corporation of Greece-Exploration & Exploitation of Hydrocarbons SA (DEP-EKY) will sign agreements with units of Enterprise Oil Plc, Union Texas Transnational and Triton International Petroleum Co, the ministry said.
The three were chosen in December 1996 after a tender. Development Minister Vasso Papandreou said at that time that DEP-EKY would retain a 12 percent interest in each consortium.
Prospecting licenses would cover "extensive research projects for the next six to seven years, with initial research investments totalling over $100 million", last December's announcement said.

Enterprise and Union Texas will prospect in the area of the northwestern Peloponnese and Epirus, south of Albania, with the former company as operator. The total exploration spending will be $26 million for the Peloponnese and $20 million for Epirus.
Triton will prospect the western gulf of Patras, and the western part of mainland Greece, spending a total of $26 million for the Patras area and $35 million for western Greece.

According to ministry estimates, if at least two oil fields "of average size" are discovered, total investment for exploitation would amount to about $1 billion. Two fields of that size would be enough to cover about 20 percent of the country's oil needs and produce total revenue for the government of $1.5 billion, the ministry said. --Artemis Hionides, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
